title: Console → Cost Model API Integration Plan (v1) — checklist + feature flags + rollout
content:
Context
- Console cost views currently compute “cost” via a mix of telemetry aggregations + legacy pricing hooks. This leads to inconsistencies vs Optimize and (sometimes) invoice totals.
- Goal of this work: Console backend uses the standard Cost Model API (v1) for request-attributed cost primitives + breakdown taxonomy.
- Non-goal: change billing system of record. Console should display cost-model outputs clearly and label anything that is “estimated” or “allocated”.

Owners / reviewers
- Console integration lead: Chloe Martin
- Console backend architecture: Jada Williams
- Console dashboards: Felix Schneider
- Cost Model API lead: Ethan Park
- Aggregation/perf: Thomas Baird
- SRE: Rafael Mendes

Scope (Console v1)
In scope
1) Console “Cost breakdown” pages (per route / per model / per workspace) should source breakdown rows from Cost Model API.
2) Console “per-request cost estimate” used in traces/details view (where available) should call Cost Model API estimate endpoint.
3) Add feature-flagged fallback behavior (old pipeline) if Cost Model API is degraded.
4) Add monitoring to track:
   - API call volume + latency from Console
   - Flag exposure and adoption
   - Drift vs observed spend (via shared dashboards, not computed in Console)

Out of scope (v1)
- Customer-facing pricing calculator logic
- Replacing existing invoice totals or customer billing PDFs
- Deep what-if UI in Console (Optimize owns)

Dependencies / prerequisites
- Cost Model API deployed to dev/staging/prod with tenancy/auth ready (Kaitlyn + Ethan).
- Schema version negotiation supported in client library (ENG-4830 / PR-28462).
- Telemetry inputs stabilized for prefill/decode + KV cache metrics (runtime + telemetry leads).
- Grafana dashboards for cost-model service are live (observability pack PR-391).

Integration approach (high level)
- Console backend will call Cost Model API server-to-server.
- Console does NOT compute cost primitives locally (except for minor presentation formatting).
- Console caches responses for hot dashboard queries (bounded TTL) to avoid cost-model service becoming the hot path bottleneck.
- Console explicitly passes:
  - workspace_id / tenant
  - time window + aggregation granularity
  - breakdown dimensions requested (bounded)
  - desired schema version (with fallback)

Endpoints used by Console (v1)
(Names are conceptual; final is per design spec)
1) GET/POST /internal/cost-model/v1/breakdown
   - Used for dashboard tables/charts
   - Must be bounded: limit #rows, explicit group_by, explicit time bucket
2) POST /internal/cost-model/v1/estimate
   - Used for request details/traces view or near-real-time per request

Console should not call /what-if endpoints.

Feature flags
Primary flags
1) console.cost_breakdown.use_cost_model_api
   - Default: OFF
   - Gates dashboard queries to Cost Model API.
   - When OFF: use existing cost aggregation pipeline.
2) console.cost_breakdown.cost_model_api_shadow_mode
   - Default: ON in staging only
   - When ON: call Cost Model API in parallel, compare results, but display legacy results.
3) console.cost_breakdown.disable_cost_model_on_error
   - Default: ON
   - If Cost Model API errors/timeouts exceed thresholds, auto-disable integration at runtime (circuit breaker behavior).
4) console.cost_breakdown.schema_version_pin
   - Default: “v1” (explicit)
   - Allows pinning/rolling schema versions safely.

Flag evaluation
- Evaluate per workspace_id (tenant) + environment.
- Start with Redwood internal workspaces only (dogfood allowlist).

Fallback behavior
- If Cost Model API is unavailable or times out:
  - Serve legacy cost breakdown pipeline results.
  - Display a subtle internal-only warning banner (staff-only) in staging during rollout.
  - Emit metric: console.cost_model.fallback_used = 1 with reason.
- If API returns “unsupported schema version”:
  - Retry with negotiated version via client library.
  - If still unsupported, fallback to legacy pipeline and page on-call only if sustained.

Timeouts / retries / budgets (Console caller)
- Hard timeout per request: 800ms (staging), 500ms (prod) for breakdown endpoint calls.
- Retries: max 1 retry, only on idempotent requests and only for 5xx/UNAVAILABLE; jittered backoff.
- Circuit breaker:
  - Open if error rate > 5% over 2 minutes OR p95 latency > 1.5s over 5 minutes.
  - While open: skip API calls for 10 minutes, serve legacy.

Caching strategy (Console)
Goal: reduce repeated identical calls from dashboard refreshes.
- Cache key: (workspace_id, time_range, bucket, group_by, filters, schema_version)
- TTL guidelines:
  - last_1h / last_6h: 30–60s TTL
  - last_24h: 2–5 min TTL
  - last_7d / last_30d: 10–30 min TTL
- Cache size limits: cap by workspace to prevent noisy neighbor behavior.
- Never cache error responses.

Request bounding rules (Console responsibilities)
To prevent cardinality blowups (per API guidelines):
- Always specify:
  - time window start/end
  - time bucket size (e.g., 1m/5m/1h)
  - group_by dimensions (max 2 in v1)
  - max_rows (e.g., 200)
- Disallow in Console UI for v1:
  - arbitrary grouping by request_id at high volume
  - unbounded dimension combos (model_version x route x region x quant_profile x …)
- Prefer “top K + other” patterns where needed.

Data mapping (Console UI fields → Cost Model fields)
Console expects to render a breakdown table roughly:
- Total cost
- Compute cost (GPU/accelerator)
- Prefill vs decode split
- Cache hit/miss impact (where applicable)
- Overhead allocated (explicitly labeled)
- Confidence / quality notes (if present)

Mapping rules
- Console displays the taxonomy rows returned by Cost Model API verbatim (names from taxonomy), with stable ordering.
- Console must not re-classify rows (avoid drift).
- Any “allocated” categories must be labeled in UI as “Allocated overhead (policy-based)” with tooltip link to internal doc (for now).

Shadow mode validation plan (staging)
Target: verify correctness + stability before turning on for users.
Steps
1) Enable console.cost_breakdown.cost_model_api_shadow_mode = ON in staging for internal workspaces.
2) For each dashboard request:
   - Call legacy pipeline + Cost Model API
   - Compare:
     a) Total cost delta percentage
     b) Breakdown row presence + ordering
     c) Prefill/decode split sums
3) Emit metrics:
   - console.cost_model.shadow.delta_total_pct (histogram)
   - console.cost_model.shadow.missing_rows_count
   - console.cost_model.shadow.schema_version
4) Acceptance thresholds (initial)
   - Median absolute delta <= 3%
   - p95 absolute delta <= 10%
   - Missing rows == 0 for v1 required taxonomy
5) Investigate deltas above thresholds with Telemetry + Cost Model owners. Common causes:
   - telemetry lag
   - quant profile mislabeling
   - KV cache hit-rate mismatch
   - legacy pipeline bug/assumption mismatch

Rollout plan by environment
Dev
- Goal: unblock rapid iteration.
- Flags:
  - use_cost_model_api: ON for all dev tenants
  - disable_cost_model_on_error: ON
- Validate:
  - basic rendering
  - schema negotiation works
  - bounded requests are enforced

Staging
Phase 0: shadow-only (1–3 days)
- cost_model_api_shadow_mode: ON
- use_cost_model_api: OFF
- Monitor deltas and API performance.

Phase 1: dogfood (2–5 days)
- use_cost_model_api: ON for allowlist (Redwood internal workspaces)
- Keep shadow comparisons running in background for non-allowlisted staging tenants.

Prod
Phase 0: dark launch (no user impact)
- use_cost_model_api: OFF
- Enable health-check pings from Console to Cost Model API (low volume).

Phase 1: internal allowlist (24–48h)
- use_cost_model_api: ON for Redwood internal workspaces only.
- Strict fallback: if error/latency, immediately revert to legacy.

Phase 2: small external ramp (2–4 days)
- 5% of workspaces (randomized, exclude known high-volume tenants initially).
- Success gate: no increase in Console p95 latency attributable to cost endpoints; Cost Model API within SLO; fallback rate < 1%.

Phase 3: medium ramp (3–7 days)
- 25% of workspaces
- Include at least:
  - one Dedicated tenant
  - one Private/VPC tenant
  - multiple hosted regions

Phase 4: full rollout
- 100% of workspaces
- Keep legacy pipeline available for 2 release cycles behind a kill switch.

Rollback plan
When to rollback
- Console user-facing dashboards show missing/incorrect rows (severity: high)
- Cost Model API p95 latency causes Console dashboard timeouts
- Drift alert indicates systemic mismatch tied to schema release

How to rollback
- Flip console.cost_breakdown.use_cost_model_api = OFF globally.
- Keep shadow mode OFF during incident unless explicitly needed (avoid extra load).
- Create an incident note with:
  - timeframe
  - affected tenants
  - error codes
  - schema versions

Observability checklist (must-have before prod ramp)
Console-side metrics
- console.cost_model.request.count (by endpoint, status)
- console.cost_model.request.latency_ms (p50/p95)
- console.cost_model.fallback_used (by reason: timeout, 5xx, schema)
- console.cost_model.shadow.delta_total_pct (staging)
- console.cost_model.response.rows_returned (to detect bounding regressions)

Dashboards / alerts (who owns)
- Cost Model API service dashboards: Platform/SRE (Rafael)
- Console dashboard latency impact: Console on-call (Chloe/Jada)
- Drift monitoring: Telemetry/Analytics + Finance visibility

Security / tenancy checklist
- Use service-to-service auth (mTLS + internal identity).
- Ensure workspace_id scoping is enforced on server side.
- No PII in requests beyond identifiers already used in Console backend.
- Log redaction: do not log raw filter values if they could include customer-provided route names with sensitive context (keep hashed/normalized).

Release coordination
- Bundle with Console release train (Connor O’Brien).
- Schema changes must be backward compatible during rollout windows; pin schema version until verified.

Open questions / risks
1) Overhead allocation presentation
- Finance wants overhead allocation visible (explicit line item). Console needs UX copy to avoid “why doesn’t this match invoice?” confusion.
- Action: Marissa + Chloe to confirm tooltip wording and link.

2) Telemetry lag → false drift / confusing UI
- If telemetry inputs lag, Cost Model API may return partial windows.
- Action: cost-model API should return “data_freshness” indicator; Console should show “data delayed” banner (internal first).

3) Cardinality explosion from new UI filters
- Risk: product asks for more grouping dimensions.
- Action: enforce request bounding at API and in Console UI; revisit in v2 with pre-aggregation.

4) Schema evolution
- Console must be resilient to new optional rows/fields.
- Action: treat unknown breakdown rows as displayable; do not hard-fail rendering.

Implementation checklist (Console backend)
- [ ] Add cost-model client lib dependency (ENG-4830)
- [ ] Implement request builders for breakdown + estimate endpoints
- [ ] Enforce bounding rules (max_rows, group_by limits)
- [ ] Add caching layer + TTL policy
- [ ] Add feature flags + allowlisting
- [ ] Add fallback path to legacy pipeline
- [ ] Add metrics + traces (include schema_version)
- [ ] Stage shadow mode comparison + reporting
- [ ] Staging dogfood validation complete + sign-off from Ethan + Rafael
- [ ] Production ramp plan scheduled + comms in #eng-platform and #product

Sign-off criteria (before Phase 2 in prod)
- Cost Model API SLOs met for 7 consecutive days (per SRE)
- Staging shadow deltas within thresholds for 72 hours
- Console fallback rate < 0.5% during internal allowlist
- No P0/P1 incidents attributed to cost model integration during internal phase
